title: Laboratory Contamination

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: The unintended introduction of unwanted microorganisms, chemicals, or foreign material into a culture, reagent, or sample.
explanation: Contamination can be biological (an unwanted organism growing in or alongside your culture), chemical (a reagent cross-contaminated with another substance), or cross-contamination between samples via shared equipment or aerosols. Recognizing it (e.g. unexpected colony morphology, cloudiness in a broth that should be clear, unexpected biochemical results) and tracing its likely source (technique lapse, contaminated reagent, contaminated equipment) is a core lab skill, addressed largely through consistent aseptic technique.
commonMisconceptions: Assuming contamination is always obvious to the eye — a contaminating organism with similar colony morphology can go unnoticed without careful technique.
